spec_match.rationale: Side-by-side of the explainer's core promise: real menubar/menulist/menuitem markup (ID-reference commandfor wiring, valid across dev-trial iterations) against the hand-rolled APG menubar pattern the elements replace — roving tabindex, aria-expanded/haspopup, Escape/arrow keyboard model per the ARIA Authoring Practices.

interactive.rationale: Both panels are fully drivable; every activation (pointer or keyboard) lands in a live ledger; the APG panel implements the complete keyboard model.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises live native markup beside a working APG implementation; delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: Disabled items handled in both panels (native disabled attribute; APG aria-disabled with blocked activation logged); outside-click closes APG menus; the native panel's banner distinguishes early vs current iterations.

references.rationale: Feature index cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5206029088063488 and the APG menubar pattern this page implements manually.

conformance.rationale: The suite's core-trio and implicit-popover assertions are the native panel's foundations.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP: bare run drove the APG panel fully by keyboard — ArrowRight roved File→View, Enter opened with focus on first item, ArrowDown roved, Escape closed restoring invoker focus, disabled activation blocked, ledger recorded each; flag run (--enable-blink-features=MenuElements) really opened the native File menulist as a popover from its menuitem and activated New into the ledger, with the early-iteration banner correctly displayed. Zero console errors; 0px overflow both classes; screenshots read (flag-run screenshot shows the native menu open).

design_system.rationale: Panels bordered on ivory; APG dropdowns use border+stone shadow; focus outlines use --accent-blue at 2px; CSS variables only; APG buttons override background AND color explicitly.

accessibility.rationale: APG panel is the accessibility demonstration itself: role=menubar/menu/menuitem, aria-haspopup/expanded maintained live, roving tabindex, visible focus, aria-disabled honored; ledger is role=log aria-live; both menubars carry aria-labels.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Bars wrap in flex; dropdowns anchored within panels; 0px overflow at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×2000.

openQuestions.title: Native menulist does not close on item activation in the early build
openQuestions.detail: Flag-run evidence: after activating 'New', native-file still matched :popover-open — the close-on-activate behavior specified in the explainer isn't in the 141-era iteration. Re-test on a current-surface build and, if it closes there, note the build delta on the page.

openQuestions.title: Native keyboard model untested
openQuestions.detail: The explainer's arrow-key/single-tab-stop model for the native panel needs a current-surface build to verify; only pointer activation was exercised under the flag here.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible menu menubar keyboard roving tabindex popover dropdown
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Menus need the full APG keyboard model, maintained ARIA states, and restored focus on close.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The APG panel implements exactly this and the harness drove every key path.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Tether overlays to invokers and keep them within the viewport.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: APG dropdowns are position:absolute under their invoker inside the panel; native menulists use the element's own implicit anchor. Verified 0px overflow at 360px.

summary: Verified headlessly (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): the APG panel's complete keyboard model was driven end-to-end on the bare engine, and the flag run proved the native panel is real — menuitem click opened the menulist popover and activations ledgered — surfacing a genuine early-build gap (no close-on-activate) now recorded as an open question.
